What Makes a Diamond the Most Expensive in the World?

When people ask what is the most expensive diamond in the world is, they usually expect a single name. But the reality is more nuanced. A diamond doesn’t become the most valuable diamond in the world because of just one factor. It’s a combination of rarity, quality, and story. Here’s what actually drives those record-breaking prices.

Carat Weight: Bigger Isn’t Enough, But It Matters

Size is the first thing people notice. Larger diamonds are naturally rarer, which is why high-carat stones often dominate the list of the most expensive diamonds in the world category. But here’s the catch: a big diamond with poor clarity or dull color won’t command a top price. Carat weight only becomes valuable when the other qualities are equally strong. A flawless 50-carat diamond will always outperform a flawed 100-carat stone in value.

Color: The Real Game-Changer

Most people think colorless diamonds are the most valuable, but in reality, fancy-colored diamonds often take the top spot. Pink, blue, and red diamonds are incredibly rare, and rarity drives price.

For example, vivid pink and deep blue diamonds have sold for record-breaking prices because they’re nearly impossible to find in nature. That’s why many of the contenders for the most valuable diamond in the world are not white, but intensely colored.

Clarity: Flawless Means Priceless

Clarity refers to how free a diamond is from internal inclusions or external blemishes. The fewer imperfections, the higher the value. At the top end of the market, buyers expect near-perfect clarity.

A diamond that is internally flawless becomes extremely rare, especially as the size increases. Combine high clarity with large carat weight and rare color, and you’re looking at a serious contender for the most expensive diamond in the world title.

Cut: Where Beauty Meets Precision

Cut is often underestimated, but it directly impacts how a diamond reflects light. Even a high-carat, high-clarity diamond can look lifeless if it’s poorly cut.

An excellent cut maximizes brilliance and fire, making the diamond visually stunning. This is critical because buyers paying millions aren’t just buying rarity, they’re buying visual perfection.

Historical Significance: The Hidden Multiplier

This is where things get interesting. Some diamonds are valuable not just because of their physical properties, but because of their history.

A diamond owned by royalty or linked to a famous event can dramatically increase in value. In fact, historical importance can push a stone beyond what its technical qualities alone would justify. That’s why certain diamonds are considered the most valuable diamonds in the world, even if they aren’t the largest or the most flawless.

The Reality Check

If you’re trying to figure out what the most valuable diamond in the world is, stop looking for a single rule. There isn’t one. The highest-priced diamonds sit at the intersection of all these factors: size, rare color, exceptional clarity, perfect cut, and often a story that no other stone can replicate.

Miss one of these, and the value drops. Hit all of them, and you’re looking at a diamond that can break records.



Which Diamond Is the Most Expensive Ever Sold?

If you're trying to answer which diamond is most expensive, you need to separate hype from actual auction records. The title of the costliest diamond in the world (in terms of confirmed sale price) isn’t based on legends or royal history; it’s based on hard numbers from auctions. Here are the diamonds that have actually defined what a world costly diamond looks like.

The Pink Star Diamond – The True Record Holder

The Pink Star Diamond holds the official record as the most expensive diamond ever sold at auction. It was sold for around $71.2 million, and there’s a reason it dominates this list.

  • Weight: 59.60 carats
  • Color: Fancy Vivid Pink
  • Clarity: Internally flawless

Here’s the reality: pink diamonds of this size and purity are almost nonexistent. This wasn’t just a big diamond, it was a statistical anomaly. That’s why, when people ask what is the most expensive diamond in the world, this is the most accurate answer based on actual sales data.

The Oppenheimer Blue – The Blue Diamond Benchmark

Before the Pink Star took over, the Oppenheimer Blue Diamond set the benchmark for blue diamonds.

  • Price: ~$57.5 million
  • Weight: 14.62 carats
  • Color: Fancy Vivid Blue

Now here’s where people get it wrong: this diamond is much smaller than the Pink Star, yet still insanely valuable. Why? Vivid blue diamonds are rarer than most other types.

So if you’re judging purely by rarity per carat, this could still be argued as one of the most valuable diamonds in the world, even if it’s not the highest total sale.

The Hope Diamond – Priceless, But Not Auctioned

The Hope Diamond complicates the conversation.

  • Weight: 45.52 carats
  • Color: Deep blue
  • Estimated Value: $200–250 million (not officially sold)

Here’s the truth: the Hope Diamond is often called the costliest diamond in the world, but that’s technically misleading. It hasn’t been sold in a modern auction, so its value is estimated, not proven.

What makes it special isn’t just the diamond itself, it’s the story. Centuries of history, ownership by royalty, and its “cursed” reputation make it culturally priceless. If it were ever sold, it could easily become the world costly diamond by a huge margin.

So, Which Diamond Is Actually the Most Expensive?

Let’s be direct:

  • By confirmed sale price: Pink Star Diamond
  • By rarity and prestige: Oppenheimer Blue competes strongly
  • By estimated historical value: Hope Diamond could surpass all

If you're looking for a clear answer to which diamond is most expensive, the Pink Star wins. But if you’re looking at the bigger picture of value, rarity, and legacy, the conversation isn’t that simple.


Top 7 Most Expensive Diamonds in the World

If you’re searching for the costliest diamond or trying to identify the most valuable diamond in the world, this list gives you a clear, no-nonsense breakdown. These diamonds aren’t just expensive, they’re rare, historically significant, and in some cases, completely unmatched.

1. Pink Star Diamond

Price: ~$71.2 million
Unique Feature: Largest internally flawless fancy vivid pink diamond ever sold

This is the benchmark. If someone asks for the costliest diamond in the world, this is the most accurate auction-based answer.

2. Cullinan Diamond

Price: Priceless (estimated over $400 million for all parts)
Unique Feature: Largest rough diamond ever discovered (3,106 carats)

The Cullinan wasn’t sold as a single stone. It was cut into multiple gems, including the Great Star of Africa. In terms of historical and material value, it easily qualifies as one of the most valuable diamonds in the world.

3. Koh-i-Noor Diamond

Price: Priceless (no official sale value)
Unique Feature: One of the most famous and controversial diamonds in history

You can’t assign a real price to the Koh-i-Noor because it has never been sold in a modern market. Its value comes from centuries of history, making it one of the most valuable diamonds in the world beyond just money.

4. Hope Diamond

Price: Estimated $200–250 million
Unique Feature: Rare deep blue color with legendary “curse” history

Technically not auctioned in modern times, but its estimated value puts it in the top tier of any world costly diamond discussion.

5. Blue Moon Diamond

Price: ~$48.4 million
Unique Feature: Exceptional vivid blue color with flawless clarity

This diamond set a record for price per carat, which is often a more important metric than total price when judging the costliest diamond category.

6. Graff Pink Diamond

Price: ~$46 million
Unique Feature: Intense pink color with historic ownership

Pink diamonds dominate the high-value space, and this one proved that even slightly smaller stones can still rank among the most valuable diamonds in the world.

7. Regent Diamond

Price: Estimated over $60 million
Unique Feature: Flawless white diamond with royal French history

Unlike many modern auction diamonds, the Regent’s value is deeply tied to its association with French royalty and historical events.

Final Takeaway

If you’re expecting one clear winner for the costliest diamond, the Pink Star leads in auction price. But if you factor in history, rarity, and cultural significance, multiple stones compete for the title of the most valuable diamond in the world.

That’s the key mistake most people make, they think value is just about price. In reality, it’s a mix of rarity, story, and market demand.



Are Lab-Grown Diamonds Valuable Too?

Short answer: yes, but not in the same way as natural diamonds. If you’re comparing them purely on resale or rarity, lab-grown diamonds don’t compete. But if you’re looking at real-world use, design, and value for money, they make a strong case.

Natural vs Lab-Grown: What’s the Actual Difference?

Chemically and visually, lab-grown diamonds are identical to natural ones. Same sparkle, same hardness, same structure. The difference is origin.

  • Natural diamonds take billions of years to form and are limited in supply
  • Lab-grown diamonds are created in controlled environments within weeks

That difference in rarity is exactly why natural stones dominate the “most valuable diamond in the world” conversation. Lab-grown diamonds aren’t rare, so they don’t appreciate in value the same way.

Affordability vs Rarity: Where Lab-Grown Wins

Here’s where you need to be practical. Most people are not buying diamonds as museum pieces or auction assets. They’re buying for wear.

Lab-grown diamonds typically cost 60–80% less than natural diamonds of similar quality. That means:

  • You can afford a bigger stone
  • You can prioritize better clarity and cut
  • You don’t compromise on appearance

So while they may never be the costliest diamond, they offer something more relevant to most buyers: accessibility.

Everyday Luxury: The Real Advantage

This is where lab-grown diamonds actually make more sense than natural ones.

Spending millions on a rare diamond is a status move. But wearing diamonds daily? That’s a lifestyle choice. Lab-grown diamonds fit that perfectly.

For modern buyers looking for elegance without extreme pricing, a lab grown diamond necklace offers a smart alternative. You get the same visual brilliance without tying up a huge budget in a single piece.

Similarly, a lab grown tennis bracelet delivers the kind of shine and consistency that works for both daily wear and occasions, without the stress of wearing something overly expensive.

The Honest Take

If your goal is investment or rarity, lab-grown diamonds are not the answer. Their supply can increase, which limits long-term price growth.

But if your goal is to actually wear and enjoy your jewellery, they’re hard to beat. You’re getting the look and feel of high-end diamonds, without paying for geological scarcity that doesn’t really impact your day-to-day experience.

How to Choose Diamond Jewellery Inspired by the World’s Most Valuable Diamonds?

Looking at the most valuable diamond in the world is exciting, but copying that exact level of rarity or price isn’t realistic. What you can do is borrow the design principles behind those diamonds and apply them smartly to your own jewellery choices.

Focus on Timeless Styles, Not Trends

The biggest mistake people make is chasing trends. The diamonds that become the costliest diamond aren’t trendy, they’re timeless.

What actually works:

  • Solitaire settings
  • Clean cuts (round, oval, emerald)
  • Minimal metal distraction

These designs don’t age. That’s exactly why high-value diamonds are usually set in simple, classic styles. The focus stays on the stone, not the design noise.

Daily Wear vs Statement Pieces

You need to be honest about how you’ll actually use your jewellery.

  • Daily wear: Go for lightweight, versatile pieces that you won’t hesitate to wear regularly
  • Statement pieces: Bigger, bolder designs meant for occasions, not everyday use

Trying to turn a statement piece into daily wear usually backfires. It either feels impractical or just sits in your locker.

If you want subtle luxury, explore diamond earrings for everyday wear that balance elegance and comfort. They give you that polished look without feeling overdone.

Budget-Friendly Luxury: Think Smart, Not Cheap

There’s a difference between cutting costs and making smart choices.

You don’t need the most valuable diamond in the world to achieve a premium look. What you need is:

  • Good cut quality (this impacts sparkle the most)
  • Balanced size (not oversized just for show)
  • Clean, wearable design

That combination gives you the feel of luxury without wasting money on factors that don’t improve how the piece actually looks when worn.

For a classic high-value look, solitaire diamond jewellery remains the closest inspiration to the world’s most expensive diamonds. It’s simple, focused, and always relevant.

The Straight Truth

Most people get distracted by size and price tags. That’s not how high-value jewellery works. The diamonds that become iconic aren’t loud, they’re precise, rare, and well-presented.

If you apply that mindset, even a modest budget can give you jewellery that looks refined instead of forced.


Final Thoughts: The True Value of Diamonds

When people search for the most expensive diamond in the world, what they’re really chasing isn’t just a number, it’s the idea of ultimate rarity and perfection. But here’s the reality: price alone doesn’t define value.

Emotional Value vs Investment Value

Diamonds sit in a unique space. On one side, they can be assets, rare stones that appreciate over time and become part of elite collections. On the other, they’re deeply personal. Engagement rings, gifts, milestones, these carry emotional weight that no auction price can measure.

The most valuable diamond in the world might sit in a museum or private vault, but for most people, the diamond they wear daily holds far more meaning.

Rarity vs Accessibility

Natural diamonds dominate the conversation around rarity. That’s why record-breaking stones command massive prices, they are limited, unpredictable, and impossible to replicate naturally.

But accessibility is changing the game. Today, buyers have more options than ever. You don’t need access to the most expensive diamond in the world to own something beautiful, well-crafted, and meaningful. The market has shifted from exclusivity-only to a balance between luxury and practicality.

How Modern Buyers Define “Valuable”

This is where the biggest shift is happening. Value is no longer just about scarcity or price tags.

Modern buyers are asking:

  • Does it fit my lifestyle?
  • Can I wear it regularly?
  • Is it worth what I’m paying for how I’ll use it?

That’s a smarter approach. Instead of chasing the most valuable diamond in the world, people are choosing pieces that deliver both aesthetic appeal and real usability.

The Bottom Line

The diamonds that break records will always exist, and they’ll always grab attention. But they don’t define what’s valuable for everyone.

True value today sits somewhere in between: a balance of beauty, meaning, and practicality. Whether it’s a rare collector’s stone or a piece you wear every day, what matters is how well it fits into your life, not just how much it’s worth on paper.

For too long, the assumption in fine jewellery has been that the best things come from somewhere else - Paris, Antwerp, Geneva. Indian craftsmanship has always been world-class. What's changed is who's telling that story, and where.

The hero necklace at Cannes was designed and made in India. Every decision - the setting, the proportion, the way it sits on the body - was made here. And the diamonds in it are lab grown, which means they are physically, chemically, and optically identical to mined diamonds. The only difference is how they were created, and what that creation didn't cost.

Lab grown diamond jewellery allows us to focus entirely on the design. We're not choosing stones based on geological accident. We're choosing them because they're exactly right for the piece. That freedom shows in the work.

Why lab grown diamonds at Cannes is more than a brand moment
There will be jewellery at Cannes this year that costs more than ours. Pieces with longer histories, bigger names, older houses behind them. And we think that's exactly why this moment matters.

Lab grown diamond jewellery at one of the world's most glamorous events is a statement - not a loud one, but a real one. It says that luxury doesn't have to mean compromise. That a stone can be beautiful and brilliant and also responsibly made. That Indian craftsmanship can stand on any stage in the world and hold its own.

/blogs/lab-grown-diamond-journal-by-xazi.content:
Made in India. Made for the World.

Those five words are not a marketing line. They are a declaration - that India, the country that cuts and polishes over 90% of the world's diamonds, that carries one of the oldest jewellery traditions in human history, does not only supply the world's fine jewellery. It designs it. It names it. It wears it, on the world's greatest stages, as itself.

Think about that number. Nine in every ten diamonds that end up in a ring in Paris, a necklace in New York, or a bracelet in Tokyo - pass through the hands of a craftsman in Surat first. His hands shape the facets. His eye calibrates the symmetry. His skill transforms a rough stone into something that catches light in a way that stops a room.

And then the diamond leaves. It travels to workshops abroad, gets set under a foreign name, and enters the global luxury market - where the story told about it rarely begins with India, and rarely ends there either.
India has been the invisible hand inside every fine jewellery piece sold globally for generations. The craft has always been Indian. The story told about it, rarely so.

This is the gap that Xazina was built to close.

What lab grown diamonds change

Lab grown diamonds are not a compromise. They are, by every scientific measure, identical to mined diamonds - the same carbon structure, the same hardness, the same brilliance. The difference is origin: one is pulled from the earth at enormous environmental cost; the other is grown with precision, in a controlled environment, without the ecological and ethical complications that have followed the mined diamond industry for decades.

India leads here too. Some of the world's finest lab grown diamonds are grown and cut here. But again, the story rarely reaches the consumer with an Indian name attached to it.

Xazina changes that. Every piece is designed in India, crafted in India, certified for quality and ethics, and named by an Indian brand - one that is unapologetic about where it comes from and what it stands for.

What Cannes means

This year, Xazina’s Jewellery walks the Cannes red carpet for the first time with The True Imperfections.

This is not a vanity moment. The Cannes Film Festival red carpet is one of the most photographed and closely watched spaces in fashion and luxury. Every piece worn there becomes part of a global conversation about beauty, craftsmanship, and cultural relevance.

An Indian lab-grown diamond brand appearing on that carpet says something important: Indian luxury belongs on the world stage - not only as a supplier, but as a name, a design voice, and a creative force of its own.

This is what Made in India, Made for the World looks like when it moves beyond a slogan. A necklace under the lights of Cannes. A piece called The True Imperfections, carrying the name Xazina - and behind that name, the work of Indian craftsmen, cutters, setters, and designers who have shaped the diamond industry for generations.

It’s time we wore them.

/blogs/lab-grown-diamond-journal-by-xazi.description: The True Imperfections by Xazina: a 20ct pink-brown heart lab grown diamond necklace in 9kt rose gold, worn by Vishal Pandey at Cannes 2026.
/blogs/lab-grown-diamond-journal-by-xazi.content:
There is a 20 carat pink-brown heart sitting at the centre of a statement necklace that just walked the Cannes 2026 red carpet.

If you know diamonds, you know what that means. Pink diamonds - in any form, at any size - are among the rarest stones on earth. The brown that runs through this one doesn't diminish it. It grounds it. Pulls the blush away from precious and into something earthier, warmer, more alive. A pink-brown heart at 20 carats, in nature, is the kind of stone that takes decades to surface. If it surfaces at all.

Lab grown diamond technology changed that calculation entirely.

When Parth Gupta, Xazina's founder, set out to design the hero piece for Cannes, he didn't start with a mood board. He started with a question: what stone exists that could anchor something genuinely unlike anything else? The pink-brown heart was the answer. And because it was lab grown - chemically identical to a mined stone, created without the geological lottery - it was possible to find exactly the right one. Not the closest available. The right one.

Everything else in the piece was built around that stone.

The necklace is called The True Imperfections. 107 grams of 9kt rose gold, chosen because its warmth echoes the blush of the diamond at its centre. 486 lab grown diamonds, all round, none the same colour grade - D through H, every variation of white and warmth mixed deliberately across the piece. The vines of India's banyan tree running the full length of the gold, wild and asymmetric, the way the banyan actually grows. At the base, the gold fragments like cracked earth. At the top, it holds.

And at the centre: the heart.

The mismatched diamonds were not an oversight. They were the point.

In fine jewellery, consistency is everything - matched stones, controlled grades, perfect uniformity. The True Imperfections went the other way on purpose. Each slight variation in colour grade shifts the light differently. The piece moves. It breathes. It refuses to be still.

That's what a 20 carat pink-brown heart deserves around it. Not a perfect frame. A living one.

At Cannes Film Festival 2026, Vishal Pandey wore it on the red carpet - making Xazina India's firstlab grown diamond jewellery brand to appear there. The stone that shouldn't exist, at the centre of a lab grown diamond necklace that refused to be flawless, on the most photographed red carpet in the world.

Some things are too alive to be perfect.

The True Imperfections is a one-of-a-kind statement necklace. To enquire, reach out to us on WhatsApp.

/blogs/lab-grown-diamond-journal-by-xazi.description: From a question to his father to the Cannes red carpet, this is how Parth Gupta built Xazina into India's first lab grown diamond jewellery brand.
/blogs/lab-grown-diamond-journal-by-xazi.content:
There is a word in Hindi - Khazana - that means treasure. Not possession. Not wealth. The kind of thing that holds a feeling long after the moment has passed. Parth Gupta changed the spelling, kept the soul. And Xazina's was born.

But the story begins earlier.

Parth grew up in a family of jewellers. Diamonds were the language of his childhood. And still, one question formed that he couldn't let go of - he asked his father: why do we gift diamonds to people?

Because they're a symbol of love, his father said.

Parth thought about that. And then he thought: is it truly a symbol of love - or a symbol of destruction?

That question became the entire foundation of Xazina.

The answer he found was lab grown diamonds. Identical to mined diamonds in every measurable way - chemically, physically, optically - but created without the cost to the earth. For Parth, this wasn't a compromise. It was a liberation.

Lab grown diamonds meant designing without constraint. Sourcing exactly the right stone, not the best available one. Building an Indian luxury jewellery brand whose ethics were as considered as its craft.

That freedom showed most clearly at Cannes 2026.

The True Imperfections - a necklace of wild gold banyan vines, 486 deliberately mismatched lab grown diamonds, and a 20 carat pink-brown heart at its centre - worn by Vishal Pandey on the red carpet. Making Xazina's India's first lab grown diamond jewellery brand to appear there. A Delhi jewellery brand standing on the most photographed stage in the world.

Made in India. Made for the world.

What comes next are two new collections - still in the making. One built around design. One built around purpose. Both are rooted here. Both are made for everywhere.

The founding question hasn't changed. At Xazina's, the answer has always been love. Every piece, from the first to the one that just walked Cannes, has been about proving it.

/blogs/lab-grown-diamond-journal-by-xazi.description: Learn how to find your accurate ring size at home before ordering lab grown diamond rings online. Simple methods, no jeweller visit required - from Xazina.
/blogs/lab-grown-diamond-journal-by-xazi.content:
Ordering a lab grown diamond ring - or any cvd diamond ring - online is easy right up until you hit the size dropdown. Get it wrong and a beautiful ring turns into a resizing errand. The good news: getting an accurate ring size at home takes about five minutes and no special tools. Here's exactly how to do it.

Why Ring Size Matters More Than You'd Think
A ring that's slightly too loose will spin around your finger or slide off entirely. One that's too tight will pinch at the knuckle and leave marks by the end of the day. Unlike earrings or a pendant, a ring's fit is not something you can eyeball - it needs an actual measurement, and that measurement can shift slightly with temperature, time of day, and even how much water you've had. That's why we recommend measuring more than once before you commit to a size.

Method 1: Measure an Existing Ring
If you already own a ring that fits the finger you're buying for comfortably, this is the most reliable method.
1.    Lay the ring flat on a table.
2.    Measure the internal diameter - the distance straight across the inside of the band, in millimetres.
3.    Match that measurement to the closest size on Xazina's Size Guide.
This works especially well if you're buying a lab grown diamond engagement ring and want to confirm sizing using a ring your partner already wears often, ideally on the same finger.

Method 2: The String or Paper Strip Method
No existing ring to measure? This works just as well.
1.    Wrap a thin strip of paper or a piece of string snugly around the base of the finger.
2.    Mark the point where the ends meet with a pen.
3.    Lay the strip flat and measure the length in millimetres with a ruler.
4.    This number is your finger's circumference - use our Size Guide chart to convert it to the nearest Xazina size.

A few tips that make a real difference in accuracy: measure at the end of the day, when fingers are at their largest (not first thing in the morning); avoid measuring right after exercise or in cold weather, both of which temporarily shrink finger size; and if you're between two sizes, size up rather than down - a ring that's slightly loose is a quick, inexpensive fix, while one that's too tight usually needs a full resize.

Wide Bands Need a Size Up
If the ring you're ordering has a wider band - think eternity bands or statement solitaire settings rather than slim classic bands - go up half a size from your measured size. Wider bands sit more snugly against the finger than thinner ones, so the same internal diameter will feel tighter.

Still Not Sure? Talk to Us Before You Buy
If your measurement falls awkwardly between two sizes, or you're ordering lab grown diamond couple ring or cvd diamond couple rings and want to be doubly sure before checkout, it's worth a quick message rather than a guess. Our team can talk you through it over WhatsApp before you place the order, and every Xazina ring purchase includes lab grown diamond ring resizing support if the fit isn't quite right the first time.

A Note on Custom Pieces
If you're going the custom design route - building a bespoke engagement ring or a fully personalised piece - sizing is confirmed with you directly as part of the design process, so there's no guesswork at all. Explore custom jewellery design if that's the route you're considering.

Ready to Find Your Size?
Getting your ring size right at home takes minutes and saves you the back-and-forth of a resize later. Head to our Size Guide to match your measurement, then buy lab grown diamond jewellery with confidence that your ring will fit the way it should from the moment it arrives.

home.title: FAQs
home.html:
LAB DIAMONDS

FAQs

ASK US DIRECTLY

What makes Xazina's lab grown diamonds special?

Xazina is a lab diamond jewellery store in Defence Colony, Delhi, and every diamond we set is CVD-grown, EF colour, VVS clarity and IGI certified. Our lab diamond jewellery is set in hallmarked gold, from engagement rings to everyday pieces and custom designs. Every piece is backed by our lifetime buyback and exchange promise. Read more about Xazina's lab grown diamonds.

How do Xazina's buyback and exchange work?

Every piece of lab diamond jewellery from Xazina is covered by a lifetime buyback and an exchange or upgrade policy. You can return your jewellery for credit or trade up later. The full terms, limits and steps are on our Buyback and Upgrade page. You can also contact us or visit our store in Defence Colony, Delhi to start a request.

Are lab grown diamonds real diamonds?

Yes. Lab diamonds are real diamonds, with the same carbon crystal structure, hardness, brilliance and fire as mined diamonds. The only difference is where they form: in a controlled lab, not deep in the earth. Xazina's lab diamonds are grown by the CVD method. See how we grow and grade our diamonds.

Why choose lab grown diamonds over natural ones?

Lab diamonds give you the same look and durability at a lower price for a comparable size and quality, so you can often choose a larger or higher-grade stone. They are also traceable, since each one is grown and certified in a lab. Our lab diamond jewellery starts with timeless solitaires in The Classics and extends to coloured diamonds in Rare Hues.

Do you ship internationally?

Yes, Xazina ships internationally. Every order is insured and sent in secure packaging. Delivery times, costs and tracking details are in our Shipping Policy. For a specific destination, contact our team.

Can anyone tell the difference between lab grown and natural diamonds?

Not by eye, and not with a jeweller's loupe. Telling them apart takes specialised lab equipment. That's why every piece of Xazina lab diamond jewellery comes with an IGI report, and the report states that the diamond is laboratory grown. Learn more in our guide to lab grown diamonds.

Are lab grown diamonds IGI certified?

Xazina's lab diamonds are. IGI (International Gemological Institute) grades each stone on the 4Cs: cut, colour, clarity and carat. All of ours are EF colour and VVS clarity, and the report confirms the stone's quality and that it is lab grown. See how we use IGI certification and the 4Cs.

Where can I buy lab diamond jewellery in Delhi?

You can buy lab diamond jewellery at Xazina's store in Defence Colony, Delhi, or shop our full range online. Visit us to see our lab diamonds in person, try on engagement rings and everyday pieces, and get one-on-one guidance on your ring, your budget and your story. Book an appointment before you visit, or explore our engagement rings online. Every piece is IGI certified, with EF colour and VVS clarity.

home.title: Lab diamonds, explained
home.html:
Lab Diamond Guide

Lab diamonds, explained

Lab diamonds are real diamonds. They have the same carbon crystal structure, hardness, brilliance and fire as mined diamonds, and the only difference is where they form. Instead of deep underground over billions of years, they are grown in a controlled lab. The US Federal Trade Commission has recognised lab-grown diamonds as diamonds since 2018, and independent labs such as IGI grade and certify them on the same scale as mined stones.

How Xazina's lab diamonds are made

Every diamond we set is grown by the CVD (chemical vapour deposition) method. A thin diamond seed is placed in a chamber with carbon-rich gas, and the diamond grows layer by layer. CVD diamonds are usually Type IIa, the purest category of diamond. Read more in our guide to Xazina's lab grown diamonds.

What you get with Xazina lab diamond jewellery

  • Every stone is EF colour and VVS clarity, which means colourless to near-colourless, with no flaws visible even under 10x magnification.
  • Every stone is IGI certified, and the report states clearly that it is laboratory grown.
  • Every piece is set in hallmarked gold, from engagement rings and solitaires in The Classics to coloured diamonds in Rare Hues and everyday pieces for men in The Xazina Man.
  • Every purchase is backed by our lifetime buyback and exchange promise, and we ship internationally under our Shipping Policy.

Five questions to ask any lab diamond jeweller

  1. Is the diamond certified by an independent lab such as IGI, and can I see the report?
  2. What are the exact colour and clarity grades, not just a range?
  3. Is it CVD or HPHT?
  4. Is the gold hallmarked?
  5. What is the buyback and exchange policy in writing?

Visit a lab diamond jewellery store in Defence Colony, Delhi

See our lab diamonds in person, or design a custom piece. You can also book an appointment for one-on-one guidance on your ring, your budget and your story.
